terms.definition: The login and subscription container that holds character slots and has a clone state.
The planned placement of roles and characters across accounts based on training, simultaneous-login needs, security, cost, and operations.
An account without active Omega game time and therefore subject to current Alpha restrictions.
An additional character used for a supporting, specialized, independent, or identity-separated role.
One capsuleer identity occupying a character slot on an account.
One running instance of the EVE application connected to one logged-in account.
The account's current Alpha or Omega access state.
The character a player treats as their primary identity or progression focus; not necessarily the most skilled character for every role.
Multiple Character Training, which activates an additional simultaneous skill-training queue on the same account for a defined period; it does not allow same-account characters to log in together.
One player manually and independently operating multiple EVE clients at the same time.
An account with active Omega game time and access to Omega capabilities supported by the character's trained skills.
An item or direct purchase that makes a skill available for a character to train.
A unit of character training progress assigned to skills.
The ordered list of skills a character will train over real time.
Skills that improve fitting, capacitor, navigation, tank, targeting, weapons, or other capabilities across several ships.
Skill Points the player can apply directly to eligible skills instead of waiting for normal training.
The time a ship needs to reach the direction and speed required to enter warp.
A ship's rechargeable energy reserve used by many modules and weapons.
The fitting resource consumed by rigs.
One of the two main fitting resources consumed by installed modules.
The limit controlling which combination of drones a ship can have active.
Storage aboard a ship for assembled drones.
The range beyond a turret's optimal range where hit chance and effective damage progressively decline.
The complete combination of modules, rigs, charges, drones, and other equipment prepared for a ship and purpose.
A client mode used to test a fit without first buying or installing its parts.
The local area of space in which ships and objects can directly see and interact with one another.
Either a ship type itself or, in combat context, the final structural health layer beneath shields and armor.
Equipment installed in a ship slot to provide weapons, defenses, propulsion, electronic effects, or utility.
The distance within which a turret avoids range-based accuracy loss, before other factors such as tracking are considered.
One of the two main fitting resources consumed by installed modules.
An afterburner or microwarpdrive used to increase a ship's speed.
A fitted ship modification that uses calibration and is normally destroyed if removed.
A measure of how large a target appears to weapons and sensors; larger signatures are generally easier to hit or damage effectively.
The defenses used to absorb, resist, avoid, or repair incoming damage.
Sideways angular movement between ships that affects how well turrets can track.
A structure-related system that can move eligible personal assets when access to them is lost, subject to current rules, delays, and fees.
A saved location that a character can use for navigation or tactical positioning.
A warp-disruption field used in space where the mechanic is permitted.
The NPC enforcement organization that responds to criminal aggression in ordinary high-security space; it punishes qualifying attacks but does not guarantee prevention.
A shipboard scanner used to look for many nearby objects within a chosen range and angle without launching probes.
The protected starter region where newly created characters begin the current new-player journey.
High-security empire space governed by Crimewatch and CONCORD mechanics; it is safer than many regions but not generally free from player attack.
Low-security empire space with fewer restrictions on player combat and no CONCORD response.
Space with a security status at or below zero and broad access to player combat mechanics, including warp disruption bubbles where permitted.
A group of Triglavian-controlled systems with distinctive travel, standings, combat, and access rules.
A bookmark away from common celestial objects and travel lines, used to reduce exposure while in space; it does not create guaranteed safety.
A short restriction after certain actions that prevents another session-changing action until the timer ends.
A fixed structure that moves ships between connected solar systems.
Conditional protection and service access provided near eligible friendly structures under current mechanics.
A temporary connection between systems whose destination, lifetime, and mass capacity must be evaluated.
A visible timer created by certain actions that can restrict docking, tethering, jumping, logging off safely, or other behavior.
A formal organization made up of player corporations.
An informal or tool-supported grouping of alliances and corporations; it is not a separate in-game organization type.
An NPC- or player-run organization to which a character belongs.
A standardized set of ships, fits, skills, and operating expectations selected by a group for a purpose.
Electronic warfare: modules or effects that interfere with another ship's sensors, range, tracking, propulsion, capacitor, or combat effectiveness.
The in-game organization used to group characters for leadership, broadcasts, bonuses, movement, and coordinated activity.
The person directing a fleet's actions.
Depending on context, either moving supplies and ships or using remote-repair ships to keep fleet members alive. Clarify the intended meaning when first used.
Common shorthand for a warp disruptor or for having a target prevented from warping.
Common shorthand for a warp scrambler, which prevents warp and disables some propulsion-related functions under current mechanics.
Ships, modules, or actions used to prevent a target from escaping.
A limited-run copy of a blueprint used for manufacturing or invention and not researchable like an original.
A reusable original blueprint that can normally be researched and copied.
A fee associated with creating or modifying eligible market orders.
A market offer to purchase an item under stated price, quantity, location, and range conditions.
An in-game agreement used for item exchange, courier work, auctions, and other supported transactions.
A timed activity installed to manufacture, research, copy, invent, or react materials and blueprints.
InterStellar Kredits, the principal in-game currency.
Economic output divided by the time during which the activity actually demands the player's attention.
How readily an item can be sold near its expected price without excessive time or price reduction.
The value of the best alternative use of time, capital, characters, or assets that a choice displaces.
The extraction, processing, and transport of planetary resources through colonies managed by characters.
An in-game item with account-service and store uses that can also be traded for ISK through authorized systems.
Converting eligible items or resources into materials, subject to skills, facility, taxes, and other modifiers.
A market offer listing an item for buyers at a stated price and location.
A numerical relationship between a character and an NPC, corporation, faction, or other entity that can affect access and costs.
A site that generally appears in the probe scanner without first resolving it with scan probes.
A site or wormhole that normally must be located precisely with scan probes before warping to it.
EVE Swagger Interface, CCP's official API through which approved applications can request authorized game data.
The configurable interface that lists selected nearby objects on the current grid.
The interface used to view anomalies and signatures and to control scan probes.
Deployable probes used through the probe scanner to locate cosmic signatures or, with the appropriate type and equipment, ships and other objects.
Single Sign-On, CCP's official authorization system for signing into approved third-party applications without giving those applications the account password.
Allowing another person to access or play an account; prohibited under EVE's account rules.
Using software or automation to perform gameplay without the independent manual control required of a player.
A specific category of account or character data that a third-party application requests permission to access.
Duplicating one input across multiple clients; prohibited and never recommended by this guide.
Buying or selling in-game currency, assets, characters, or services through unauthorized real-money channels.
A security method requiring an additional authenticator or verification factor beyond the password.
